evidence: The round-0 sentence asserted "a different session in this checkout" for any mismatched assignee, which free-text assignees like `--assignee alice` falsify; by round 1 the CHANGELOG quotes the new wording "not under you" and concedes "an assignee is free text that `lit new --assignee bob` fills with a person". The fix was real, but the thread was resolved without a reply.
guidance_note: Before wording a message about a field, trace every writer of that field (here `startSpec`'s `resolveIdentity` fallback) and claim only what all of them guarantee.

evidence: The CHANGELOG claims docs/cli-reference.md states "`--assignee` does not move one", but the cli-reference text visible in F6's round-3 hunk still says nothing about `--assignee` or `start --take`. The same clause is still in the CHANGELOG verbatim at round 4 (F12-F14 hunks), so the thread was resolved silently with nothing fixed.
guidance_note: When a changelog entry names which files document a fact, grep each named file for that fact before pushing.

evidence: This re-raises F2 word for word, because F2 was never addressed: the round-1 CHANGELOG rewrite touched the F1 sentence and left the `docs/cli-reference.md ... --assignee does not move one` clause untouched. It is not caused by any fix; it is an unaddressed repeat.
guidance_note: When rewriting a changelog entry to answer one finding, re-check every other open finding anchored on the same entry in the same pass.

evidence: The only change to 08-claims-and-identity.md was a `next.go:192`->`243` line bump, while `resumeAdvice` and the identity split went undescribed. F9 re-raises it in round 3, and b04ff4d's hunk of the same paragraph is again only line bumps, so it was never addressed.
guidance_note: When a change adds behavior to machinery the doc-v1-total corpus describes line by line, update that chapter's prose in the original PR, not just its line citations.

evidence: "Three tests pin it" is stale against the four new test functions the reviewer lists. The sentence survives unchanged into rounds 3 and 4 (F10, F13), so it was never fixed. The count went stale because tests were added during review, but no single finding's fix is the cause.
guidance_note: Don't put counts of tests in a changelog; if one is written, recount it every time a test is added during review.

evidence: With `assignee != "" && assignee != actingAs`, a matching assignee also prints the lane's own sentence, so "Only an unassigned ticket prints the lane's own sentence" is false. The thread has no reply and the packet does not show whether cli-reference.md changed afterward; the CHANGELOG clause it also named was still present at round 4 (F14).
guidance_note: When documenting a boolean condition, write out its full truth table in prose (empty, matching, differing) rather than naming one branch as the only one.

evidence: The hunk adds 10 lines above `claimContext`, which shifts the `claims_context.go:101` and related citations the chapter makes. By round 4 the field had been removed (F12: claimContext "has no `actingAs` field"), which may have restored the old offsets, but the packet does not show the chapter's citations being rechecked.
guidance_note: After editing any Go file in this repo, grep doc-v1-total for `<file>:` citations and re-point every one past the edit.

evidence: This duplicates F6 and is true for the same reason: an assignee equal to actingAs takes the default sentence, as TestRunNextResumesOwnWorkInFlight shows. There is no reply, and the packet does not show the cli-reference text after round 3.

This repeats F4: chapter 08 still describes ResumedOwnWork only as "handed back to its holder". b04ff4d's chapter-08 diff at the same paragraph again changes only line numbers (`next.go:111-161`, `startAdvice` at `next.go:259`), so the gap stayed open through the last reviewed round.
guidance_note: When the same doc-gap finding comes back a second round, add the prose instead of resolving the thread silently.

evidence: The third report of the "Three tests pin it" undercount (after F5); by now there were five dedicated tests. The sentence is unchanged in the round-4 hunk, so this is an unaddressed repeat, not caused by any fix.

The comment "the reader is named only so the one ResumedOwnWork arm has an answer" says why the new `actingAs` parameter exists, not that this test covers that arm, so the reviewer overstates it; a cheap rewording would still remove the ambiguity. The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive for cause: the comment came from the agent's own decision to move actingAs off claimContext into an argument (justified in the CHANGELOG by the four gatherers), which no finding asked for.

The round-4 CHANGELOG adds "reaches the renderer as an argument rather than on the shared claim context" but keeps the older "a new `actingAs` on `claimContext`", which is a direct self-contradiction. It is drift from a mid-review redesign the agent started itself, not from a fix for any finding, so the ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag names no causing finding. The PR merged after an unreviewed round 5, so whether it was fixed is not shown.
guidance_note: When a design moves mid-PR, search the changelog entry for every sentence describing the old design and delete it in the same commit that adds the new sentence.

evidence: This is the fourth report of "Three tests pin it", now against six dedicated tests. The flag is a false positive for cause: the sentence predates review and was never edited, so this is an unaddressed repeat of F5/F10.

The clause "either one empty keeps the sentence" was true at round 0, when the condition included `actingAs != ""`. It became false when that check was dropped mid-review: F6 quotes `assignee != "" && assignee != actingAs`, and TestRenderNextOutcomeNamesTheHolderToAnUnidentifiedReader asserts the new sentence. That was a self-initiated code change, not a finding's fix, so the flag names no causing finding; F6 had already pointed at this clause in round 3.
guidance_note: When a condition loses a conjunct, grep the changelog and docs for prose that restates the old condition and update it in the same commit.

narrative: The agent never replied to any of the 14 threads; each was resolved silently. Only F1's wording fix is visible in later diffs. The CHANGELOG entry drew 8 of the 14 findings: the false `docs/cli-reference.md ... --assignee` clause and the "Three tests pin it" count were each re-raised round after round and never fixed, and mid-review redesigns (orphan clock tried and dropped, actingAs moved off claimContext, the actingAs-empty check dropped) left contradicting sentences behind. Round 1 contained nothing but an unaddressed repeat (F3). The PR used up the 5-round review cap and merged on an unreviewed round 5.
guidance_observations: Resolving threads without a reply or a fix let the same changelog defects come back for four rounds; each round billed the review again for findings already on record.
A one-paragraph changelog entry restating the design in detail became a drift surface: every mid-review design change contradicted some sentence in it.
Silent thread resolution hides from the audit trail whether a finding was fixed, rejected, or ignored, so the review gate's record is uninformative.
Hitting MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS and merging on an unreviewed head means the round-4 contradictions (F12, F14) may have shipped.

evidence: With `f.File != h.File` as an unconditional filter and Unresolved findings having File=="", `case Unresolved:` was unreachable. 602d16a replaces the filter with the ranked `answering`, handles `f.File == ""` before the verdict switch, and adds a fallback for verdicts with no case of their own.
guidance_note: For each case of a verdict switch, check that the filter in front of it can actually let that verdict through, and test each case once.

evidence: `run(root fs.FS, out *os.File, ...)` became `out io.Writer` in 602d16a, and the new main_test.go drives it through `bytes.Buffer` to cover the empty-corpus guard and the -list filter.
guidance_note: Give a new tool's `run` the same `io.Writer` signature as the sibling tools in tools/ from the start, so it can be tested.

evidence: "Does not resolve" mis-describes a filter that also lists Moved and OutOfRange. The reviewer proposed main.go's "does not hold"; the agent rightly saw that phrase was also wrong, since Unbound citations do not hold and are excluded, and aligned all three places on "judged wrong".
guidance_note: When one behavior is described in several places, write the description once from the filter's actual predicate and copy it everywhere.

evidence: A continuation citation inherits its file from prose above it, so an unrelated edit can change h.File's match and fall through to the false "no longer in the chapter" message. 602d16a ranks candidates and emits a "now resolves to X, where it recorded Y" message, covered by TestACitationThatNowResolvesToAnotherFileSaysSo.
guidance_note: When a lookup key includes a derived field (the resolved file), list the ways that field can change without the source changing before filtering on it.

evidence: Pass 2 took the first of two indistinguishable siblings. The agent took the reviewer's second option, an ambiguity note ("this is the first"), and gave a sound reason against the first: a doc line in Held's key moves on every edit above it. TestExplainSaysWhenTheSameCitationIsWrittenTwice tests both directions.
guidance_note: When a match falls back to a weaker key, count the candidates at that key and handle the more-than-one case explicitly.

evidence: The package doc and flag help said "every citation that does not hold" while the filter excludes Unbound. 602d16a rewords both to "judged wrong; one nothing can judge is not listed" and pins it with TestListPrintsTheJudgedCitationsAndNotTheUndecidedOnes.

This is the same root cause as F1, with a concrete file-rename repro that makes Explain tell the contributor to `-sync` the record away. 602d16a's TestACitationWhoseFileStoppedResolvingIsNotExplainedAsADeletedSentence encodes that exact repro.
guidance_note: Test the destructive fall-through message ("regenerate") against each way an entry can lapse, renames and deletions included, before shipping it.

evidence: `!pattern` lines were skipped with no documentation. The agent took the reviewer's "note the limitation" option, adding a doc comment in 602d16a that says which way the omission errs (re-included files read as Unresolved). That is defensible, since a partial last-match-wins matcher over unimplemented globs would answer wrongly.
guidance_note: When a parser deliberately skips a syntax form, document that and which way the skip errs in the same comment that lists the other unsupported forms.

evidence: The `-sync` help string and the `manifestPath` const both spelled out the path. False-positive flag: both lines are in the round-0 code (F2's hunk shows the same -sync help), and 602d16a changed only the -list help. a1197b9 builds the help from `manifestPath`.
guidance_note: When a constant names a path, build every user-facing string from it at the point the constant is introduced.

evidence: The Render/Regenerate code-generation path had no test. False-positive flag: that path predates review, and 602d16a's new main_test.go simply did not extend to it. a1197b9 adds a test that parses the generated Go and asserts its fields.
guidance_note: When adding a generator for a checked-in baseline, ship a test that parses its output and asserts one entry.

evidence: The reviewer's example `/home/x/proj/go.mod` stays unresolved after the fix, but a real neighbor case, `/LICENSE-REPORT.md`, was broken. The agent fixed that by trimming the slash first and declined to loosen the loop bound, citing a check of all 18 distinct absolute paths in the corpus and the risk of a deleted nested file falling back to a same-named root file. False-positive flag: `resolve` predates review.
guidance_note: When writing a path resolver with deliberate refusals, test each input shape the corpus contains (root-anchored, absolute, partial) before review.

evidence: The finding named three swallow points: `read`'s error, the WalkDir callback's per-entry `return nil`, and the discarded walk result. a1197b9 fixed the first and third but left `if err != nil { return nil }` in the callback, which F15 then flagged. `response_correct` is `no` because the plan did not cover the whole finding. False-positive flag: ignoredPaths predates review, and 602d16a only added a comment.
guidance_note: When a finding lists several swallow points, turn each into a checklist item and grep for `return nil` after `err != nil` across the whole function before claiming the fix.

evidence: The extension alternation was copied into both citeRe and pathRe, despite citeRe's own comment warning against exactly that. a1197b9 extracts `citedExt` and adds TestTheTwoPatternsAdmitTheSameFileTypes. False-positive flag: both regexes predate review.
guidance_note: When a comment warns against two copies of a pattern, check the rest of the file for a second copy of its parts before committing.

evidence: A package-level closure reached GenDecls through Inspect, so locals inside it were indexed as file declarations. a1197b9 adds `case *ast.FuncLit: return false`, and the agent also found and repaired the existing FuncDecl test, which had gone vacuous. False-positive flag: the walk predates review.
guidance_note: When excluding a scope from an AST walk, enumerate every node type that opens that scope (FuncDecl and FuncLit) and run a mutation test against each exclusion.

evidence: a1197b9, F12's named fix, kept `if err != nil { return nil }` in the WalkDir callback right under the new "Absent is an answer; unreadable is not" comment, and F12 had named that exact line. The agent conceded "it contradicted the sentence I had just added" and switched to `return err` in d2e1b2b.
guidance_note: After fixing a silent-failure finding, reread the whole function for every remaining error branch that returns nil, and test the directory-level failure as well as the file-level one.

evidence: identRe binds `store.json` on "json", so a file declaring `json` could make a drifted citation hold. The agent built that collision as a test and skipped filename tokens. False-positive flag: identsBefore/identRe predate review; a1197b9 only added `citedExt` beside them.
guidance_note: When a pattern accepts `a.b` as a qualified identifier, list the other backticked shapes the prose uses with the same form (filenames) and reject them explicitly.

evidence: `check` returns OutOfRange before reading decls, so Bound() is narrower than "names a symbol the cited file declares". The agent took the reviewer's reword option and applied it to all four places that made the claim, arguing correctly that widening Bound would change the question the 36.7% answers. False-positive flag: the CONTRIBUTING sentence is from round 0.
guidance_note: When writing a prose definition of a computed figure, derive it from the code's order of checks (early returns included) rather than from the intended meaning.

evidence: Anonymous struct fields are indexed, as the reviewer says, but unlike closure locals they are reachable (`defaults.Timeout`), so they are real declarations. The agent measured 310 such members, 4 name collisions, and a byte-identical census under the proposed exclusion, then pinned the current behavior with TestAFieldOfAnAnonymousStructIsStillADeclaration. The reviewer framed this as the F14 gap again; it is not the same gap, so caused_by is null.

BuildGlossary's `len(paths) != 1` guard had no test and could be deleted with everything still green. 0ea3bfc adds a two-sided test (ambiguous `sync.go` omitted, unique `rank.go` kept), and the guard's mutation fails only that test. False-positive flag: BuildGlossary predates review.
guidance_note: Give every refusal guard a test whose fixture reaches the guard, paired with a success case so it cannot pass vacuously.

narrative: Nearly every finding in this new-tool PR was a real defect or gap in code written before review. Despite the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags on rounds 1-3, only F15 was caused by a fix: a1197b9 answered F12 but left the WalkDir callback's `return nil` that F12 had named. Every reply tested the reviewer's claim and checked it against the corpus. The agent declined proposals that would have broken deliberate rules (F11's loop bound, F18's exclusion) with measurements, and caught a test that had gone vacuous (F14). Rounds 2 and 3 each still had fix-independent findings, so no round was avoidable, and round 4 approved.
guidance_observations: Measuring against the corpus before accepting or declining (F11, F16, F18) turned contested findings into settled ones with no follow-up rounds.

Most round 1-3 findings were pre-existing gaps in the original 4,479-line diff (untested generator, duplicated regex fragment, unhandled FuncLit, untested glossary guard); a test for each refusal and generator before the first review would have removed most of them.
The one fix-caused finding came from fixing a multi-part finding piecemeal; treating each named swallow point as a checklist item would have closed it in one round.
